findings.title: Mutating APIs allow omission of the external head pin, permitting rollback to forget a spent target
findings.evidence: audit/reserve/result default pinned_head to None; _state checks rollback only when non-None; synthetic_call invokes reserve/result without pins. In a NEW fictional fixture, completed synthetic_call returned sequence2 and conservativeCalls69. Deleting its complete events+receipts suffix then constructing a fresh Journal caused explicit audit(savedHead) to reject rollback, but ordinary synthetic_call for the SAME target succeeded again at sequence2/conservativeCalls69. No real targets or prior state were used or changed.
findings.impact: The ordinary public synthetic execution path can forget a permanently spent target and cumulative budget after complete suffix loss. The existing regression checks only opt-in pinned audit, so it does not enforce the prospective mandatory external-head requirement at mutation/dispatch boundaries. Real-source containment remains intact because all397 real targets are held and no source integration exists.
findings.trigger: Before final local synthetic repair PASS and before any future acquisition integration
findings.nextAction: Require a valid independently held current head pin for every mutating API and synthetic_call, reject omission/None/malformed/stale pins before reserving or producing work, carry the returned intent head into immediate result persistence, and add restart/suffix-loss/missing-pin mutation regressions. Preserve this candidate, manifest and finding before remediation; freeze a new candidate for independent recheck.
